2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that 2.65½ acres of nal, chala and ditch land belonging to the appellant have been acquired under the provisions of the (Emergency) Requisition of property Act. The Collector of Dhaka by order dated 02.11.88 assessed compensation at 9,63,500/-. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated. 2.11.88 the appellant filed Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988 before the Subordinate Judge and Arbitration Court, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge and Arbitration Court by the impugned order dated 23.4.91 revised the compensation assessed by the Collector of Dhaka and assessed compensation at Tk. 29,51,633.38 in all. 

 3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dt. 23.4.1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988 the appellant (requiring body) preferred Civil Revision being Civil Revision No. 740 of 1991 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. 

 7. During the course of hearing it transpired that the instant appeal arises out of First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 740 of 1991 which arose out of Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988. That very arbitration case was the subject matter of First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 744 of 1991 which was heard and dismissed by the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 28.8.1991 along with other similar cases, which on appeal before this Division was heard along with other similar matters in Civil Appeal Nos. 174-177 of 2000.Civil Appeal No. 175 of 2000 arose from Civil Petition for Leave to. Appeal No. 58 of 1995 which arose out of First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 744 of 1991 which arose out of Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988. By judgment and order dated 14.11.2012 this Division dismissed the Civil Appeal Nos. 174-177 of 2000 thereby upholding the assessment of the Subordinate Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in, inter alia, Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988, which is the source of the instant appeal before us. 

 8. Hence, the Arbitration Case No. 129 of 1988 having been elaborately discussed and dealt with in Civil Appeal No. 175 of 2000, the subject matter of the instant appeal is covered by our earlier judgment.
